These analytical methods are applied to various systems including generic chaotic systems, highly integrable systems like free theories and 1D spin chains, as well as 2/3D strongly integrable gauge theories and their corresponding dual superstring backgrounds. We employ entanglement theory to verify that our model accurately reflects the operator growth phenomenon and its eventual plateau behavior in entanglement entropy. Moreover, our analysis in a dual gauge theory system exposes the quantum dual of operator growth and operator spreading as entanglement growth among the constituent strings in the dual superstring representation.

The atomic structure of the Hoyle state, a state of incredible size and a key aspect of stellar carbon nucleosynthesis, can be understood through measurements taken using a highly advanced, large-scale detector called the FRAM-ABC experiment. By precisely analyzing the decay products of the Hoyle state and accounting for the effect of Coulomb interaction, researchers were able to determine the direct-decay contribution to the total decay and assess the accuracy of current theoretical models.

Significant breakthroughs in understanding and modeling fracture have been made
regarding the creation of intrinsic material length and time scales through the use
of non-local and phase-field models. In this investigation, we explore the role
of these inherent size and time measures in a simple 2D pre-stressed pre-cracked
plate model that incorporates both features. We find that both scale measures are
crucial in determining the transition from slow crack growth to dynamic, oscillating
crack propagation, with factors influencing the size and trajectory of resulting
crack branches. Introducing a time scale to our model reveals an enhanced
understanding of dynamic crack behavior, yielding a more concise representation
of an underlying fracture equation that depends only on these inherent size and
time measures in a size-time plane. This equation can predict and classify the
various types of crack growth observed in simulations, providing valuable insight
into fracture behavior.

In a study regarding the properties of finite-state channels with feedback and state information, it has been demonstrated that the capacity of these channels is equal to the supremum of the conditional entropies H(Y_k,Y_{k+1},...|X_k,X_{k+1},...,U_U,X_U,X_0,X_0^-,Y_U,Y_U,Y_0,Y_0^-|U_U,U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U_U,U

A novel class of superconductors with no pairing in momentum space has been theorized to exist within a specific type of magnetic environment. By developing a correlation product method that works at the level of individual electrons, we were able to confirm superconducting behavior in a two-dimensional material with spin-orbit coupling and an attractive interaction between electrons of opposite spin orientation, which creates a pairing in P-wave configuration. This confirms that a non-trivial topological state of superconductivity can be achieved under such conditions, enabling the creation of Majorana zero modes on vortices with planar spins. These V-shaped vortices exhibit unique properties including a sharp contrast in their density of states at the center when compared to a vortex with a spin-up configuration, which exhibits a dense singularities characteristic of a d-wave state.

This study focuses on understanding and interpreting tables within scientific documents, specifically requiring the abilities to verify information within these tables and locate relevant evidence. To tackle this challenge, a competition was organized as part of the 9th resource-associated semEval event, known as SEM-TAB-FACTS. The task is comprised of two interconnected sub-tasks, both of which involve classifying claims as true, false, or uncertain. The first sub-task, TAB-VERIF-YES, involves locating supporting texts for a given claim within a scientific document table, while the second sub-task, TAB-VERIF-NL, presents the claim in natural language format and still requires finding the supporting text. To facilitate this competition, a high-quality knowledge dataset was developed, consisting of over 25,000 rows of complex tabular data along with 110,00U individual cell-based claims extracted from renowned scientific journals. The corresponding code and data can be accessed at https://github.com/roberts2k/TabFact-Dataset. The results show that all participating teams successfully completed both sub-tasks, though their performances varied significantly, particularly on task 1 where a notable gap in F1 scores was observed.

This analysis explores the essential role of complex numbers in Quantum Mechanics, delving into common justifications for complex formalism and offering additional perspectives to support its necessity. By examining these factors, we hope to clarify the underlying reasoning for employing complex numbers in Quantum mechanics.

A graph G is considered fully identifiable when a subset of its vertices R can pinpoint each vertex uniquely by determining their distance to every point in R. A sub-set of R that does this best with the fewest points is known as the minimum identifying set or "metric dimension" of the graph. Here we discuss the version of this property where the shortest distance between any two points in the graph is capped at some number k and how it affects the identification of points by a sub-set of R that does this best with the fewest points.

These notes document my progression through the equations governing distant groundwater movement and the dynamics of water tables as described in Equation A-1 through A-22 of Witherspoon et al.'s "Equations of Groundwater Movement" (1966), along with the referenced "Equations of Groundwater Movement" by Freeze and Logan (1964). The documentation aims to aid in verifying a code I'm developing for simulating groundwater flow.

This work has investigated the potential of flue gas treatment using ozone and ultraviolet radiation to produce sulfuric acid, which can be collected as a byproduct. A laboratory-scale system was used to optimize process conditions, focusing on the removal of sulfur dioxide, ultraviolet radiation intensity, gaseous sulfate production, and ozone efficiency. Results showed that sulfur dioxide removal reached 75% and gaseous sulfates were formed as a result of this removal process. Full removal of sulfur dioxide and maximum yield of sulfates were achieved by optimizing UV radiation and ozone levels, which in turn led to a maximum sulfate yield of 65%. Although ozone production is energy-intensive, the yield of sulfates suggests an economically viable process, positioning the system as a precursor to a potential value addition unit rather than a pollution control system.

As interest in neuromorphic computing grows, engineers face a key challenge in simulating and testing the technology before building new hardware. To overcome this challenge, the hardware engineering process relies on the SystemC hardware abstraction layer, which allows for non-systemc models to be integrated into the workflow. In this paper, a parallel SystemC hardware abstraction layer is proposed for simulating spike-ratio units, a type of efficient and scalable neuromorphic processor. To illustrate the benefits of parallel simulation, two parallel algorithms for spike-ratio units are developed and a SystemC model of a neuromorphic accelerator based on this technology is designed. A comparison of the SystemC and non-systemc models in terms of memory, execution time, and bandwidth usage is performed to highlight the advantages of the SystemC approach for large-scale neural network simulations.

Deploying machine learning in practical scenarios can often present challenges,
especially when probabilistic information about quantities is involved, which
can result in unwieldy probability distributions. This paper introduces Indecision
Trees, a novel deep learning approach that addresses the issue of quantified
predictive uncertainty. By offering a policy that guarantees at least the same level
of performance as any other action, even in the face of uncertain outcomes,
Indecision Tree models provide high-confidence, low-regret performance. These
models are especially beneficial in cases where making a single, potentially
flawed prediction isn't feasible and delivering multiple, context-dependent predictions
is preferred. Furthermore, to address the issue of explaining their reasoning,
Indecision Tree models are designed to present their arguments in a clear and
comprehensible format, making their line of reasoning easy to follow and
validate. We demonstrate the effectiveness and interpretability of our method on
two challenging datasets, namely estimating the weight of objects and providing
risk assessments for driving, outperforming conventional methods in terms of
reasoning accuracy and stability.

The DTW distance is commonly used in sequence analysis, but its time complexity is cubic, making similarity search employing the DTV distance impractical for real-world applications. Some optimizations, such as LD, have reduced its complexity to linear, yet their efficiency is hindered when dealing with time-varying sequences. Our proposed PrunedDTW offers a new CX index for similarity search with CX time, avoiding time-varying effects and eliminating the need for complex operations. CX enables a query sequence to be terminated early in abandoned situations, making CX both simple and effective. Our results show that CX outperforms existing abstractions and hybrid approaches in real-world datasets, with a particularly notable improvement on EDN, LDN, and CXNX.

Current educational tools used in testing provide frameworks that help teach core testing concepts, an area in which research is rapidly growing. Traditional feedback methods in these tools often directly show students the test cases or code defects resulting from their mistakes. However, studies in testing education have yet to thoroughly examine the effectiveness of this approach. This research aims to fill this gap by investigating the effectiveness of a novel inquiry-based learning method that asks students to figure out test cases or code defects on their own. An online teaching assistant tool has been developed to demonstrate both learning approaches for three fundamental testing concepts and a thorough comparison was conducted in a controlled setting with 80 sophomore and junior students to assess the effectiveness of these methods. Our findings reveal that the inquiry-based learning method has a significant positive impact on student learning outcomes, improves their understanding of the underlying concepts, and also has the added benefit of taking less time and being more engaging for students. These results suggest that the inquiry-based learning method can be a valuable addition to teaching testing tools in addition to the commonly used traditional feedback approach.

In domains requiring accountability, trust, and comprehension of decisions made by machines, particularly when dealing with vulnerable individuals or critical systems, it is essential to offer clear explanations of a DNN's predictions. This study introduces a novel approach to generating explanations for a DNN's concept-based activation of positive or negative ideas by merging concept analysis with inductive logic programming. This unified framework allows for the learning of explanations from both labeled and unlabeled data, while also enabling the explanation of a DNN's underlying biases. To test the efficacy of the concept analysis and inductive logic programming integration, we employed various evaluation metrics in real-world applications involving three pre-trained convolutional neural networks for image classification.

Over-smoothing significantly constrains the complexity of Graph Convolutional Networks, making it crucial to understand the root cause. A thorough examination of the over-smoothing phenomenon and Graph Convolutional Networks is presented in this article, including an estimation of the upper limit for its occurrence. The study sheds light on the pivotal elements contributing to over-smoothing and offers empirical evidence validating various countermeasures to mitigate it.

Dark matter particle research is conducted within the Standard Model effective field theory framework, focusing on the interaction of dark matter with a leptonically decaying Z boson in association with one or two blue jet particles in proton-proton collisions at the LHC. Z boson data, selected by its visible momentum and blue jet data, selected by their momenta, are analyzed from 36 fb$^{-1}$ of proton proton collisions at 13 TeV. No significant deviation from expectations is observed, setting 95% confidence level limits on cross sections and dark matter properties, including the mass, spin and couplings of the dark matter particles.

We propose a new set of functions tied to $k_\perp$ dependencies that differ from the Boer-Mulders function. These functions are connected to quark spin alignment as a collective phenomenon. Additionally, they depend on the movement of partons in the transverse direction, related to the Fock-Schwinger phase. A key difference is that, unlike the Boer-Mulders function, these new functions don't require parton correlations of longitudinal and transverse parton spins.

Homeomorphisms with compact support on a Tychonoff space can be given several equivalent topological structures by viewing them as either a union of groups of homeomorphisms with the same support size or as a subset of the group of homeomorphisms of its compactified space. A space has the CSHP if these two definitions yield the same topological space, which is the main topic of the paper's methods to prove that product spaces of specific spaces with CSHP possess CSHP.

Research into remote epitaxy on monolayer graphene has revealed that it can facilitate the growth of materials incompatible with traditional methods on sapphire. Nevertheless, understanding the mechanisms behind this phenomenon and distinguishing it from other forms of epitaxy can be challenging. In this study, researchers examined the epitaxial growth of Heusler alloys on a graphene/sapphire template. By examining the equilibrium properties of interfacial atoms through ab-initio calculations and analyzing the orientation preferences through oriented impact ionization, researchers discovered that the balance between remote epitaxy and van der Waals epitaxy is influenced by strong interactions with underlying oxygen atoms on the sapphire surface, rather than the graphene layer, thus shifting the role of carbon atoms from remote to van der Waals mediators. Furthermore, researchers observed that the growth of Heusler alloys is governed by a combination of covalent bonding with interfacial carbon atoms and kinetic factors, resulting in various orientation preferences dependent on the chemical composition of the alloy.

We analyze methods for making statistical inferences from multivariate time series data with heavy tails and non-stationary characteristics. By comparing two models, we examine how weight-coefficient and tail-index estimates change over time and time-dependent regression functions are approximated using penalized local linear estimation. To evaluate our findings, we developed simulation studies and applied our methods to analyze a data set showing the relationship between Bitcoin and national crypto regulations.

Recent observations by the James Webb Space Telescope of the massive galaxy cluster el Gordo (ACT-CL J0102$-$4915) have led to the identification of a particularly striking and highly lensed elastically connected structure. This is the first instance of a red supergiant star being identified at such a great distance through the amplification of a galaxy cluster's effect, located within a lensed structure known as EGB 1. By analyzing multiple wavelengths of light, researchers have established a highly accurate model of the cluster's influence and a precise map of the magnification it elicits. By analyzing the stellar and gaseous components of a particularly luminous star forming system, located at a great distance and magnified by a factor of 1000, scientists have determined a highly accurate estimate of its true size and mass. This precise model has enabled the identification of a massive red supergiant located at a great distance and magnified by a factor of 1000, which exhibits a remarkable level of magnification and is 1000 times more luminous than a typical red supergiant star. This remarkable object, which has been magnified by a factor of 1000, is among the most luminous red supergiant stars ever identified and is 1000 times more luminous than a typical red supergiant star. By studying this extraordinary object, researchers have gained a unique insight into the

Internet Service Providers have long struggled to address customer demands for superior quality of service, while also meeting profit needs. To address this issue, we examine collaborations between content providers and Internet service providers to enhance profit and improve quality of service for end customers. Specifically, we develop a two-stage game to content providers bidding for traffic from service providers, aiming to attract more traffic and increase profit, while providing service providers with traffic information and profit, thereby improving quality of service. We develop analytical solutions to this game, and our results indicate that such collaborations can benefit service providers and content providers, leading to increased profit and improved quality of service for end customers.

The GNS construction forms a correspondence between abstract collections of inner products with linear operations and abstract sets of measurements with associated probabilities. This correspondence has two key properties: it converts algebraic relationships in the measurement sets to corresponding relationships in the inner product collections, and vice versa. As a result, every mathematical object in one set corresponds to a unique object in the other set. This equivalence can be understood as a weaker form of equivalence, where equivalences are defined as mappings that preserve certain relationships rather than being direct mappings. This equivalence is formally represented as a functor that establishes a relationship between two categories of equivalences, and our research focuses on representing this functor, and more specifically, its inverse as a functor, for systems described by quantum mechanics.

The $\alpha$-attractor models in inflationary theory hold great promise in the context of upcoming cosmological observations, also having connections to supergravity. Exponential and polynomial models of this type are compared against recent data from the 2018 Planck release and a combined dataset encompassing Planck, BICEP2, and BICEP3 results, while also considering future CMB-S4 forecast data. The choice of $\alpha$ is determined based on these dataset constraints, with the models then evaluated for suitability based on $n_s$ and $n_{st}$ alignment with latest dataset readings and theoretical considerations. All $\alpha$-attractor models conform to the $\lambda$-potential in supergravity when the limit of large $\alpha$ is reached, with the models' predictions of potential and deviation from slow-roll also examined. An illustration of how these models may help resolve the hierarchy problem is also provided.

In the context of a hyperbolic 3-manifold defined by a specific structure and measured foliation pair on its boundary, where one element is particularly complex, we investigate its properties when close to a defined ideal geometric form. If the defined structure is in near-proximity to a different, more simplified form also defined by a specific parameter, we examine how the defined structure changes and is divided into distinct regions. Within an identified set of distinct regions, we compare these changes to those produced by a defined, measured foliation with a defined density across the boundary, while also examining the defined structure's interaction with a defined geometric mapping to a different space. Additionally, we discuss implications of this finding for the defined relationship between two defined structures and their associated geometric spaces, as well as implications for the defined relationship between a more simplified structure and its associated geometric space.

This study re-evaluates two well-established phenomena in investment analysis,
notably the phenomenon of return anomalies disappearing when employing cross-sectional methods and the phenomenon of cross-sectional return distributions being significantly skewed towards negative returns. By analyzing an general class of models, we uncover that and other phenomena can be attributed to a common source, and we establish the broadest possible conditions in which portfolio returns follow a cross-sectional negative exponential distribution.

This study investigates the impact of realistic noise on heart sound classification, treating real and simulated noise as distinct categories in a four-class problem that includes cor recte, mur correcte, noise real and noise simul. A state-of-the-art method for classifying heart sounds with simulated noise was initially introduced in our previous work. Here, we compare its performance under noisy conditions, where it surprisingly outperforms in the simulated noise category. Our proposed approach utilizes a one-dimensional Convolutional Neural Network enhanced with two innovative techniques: a depth-wise and a channel-wise technique. These techniques are convolutional dilations and a max-pooling layer, enabling the CNN to distinguish between signals and various types of noise. Our proposed method demonstrates excellent results in our experiments and is expected to contribute heart sound interpretation in telemedicine applications.

In a 2021 study, we had developed a more accurate calculation for a specific nuclear transition in $^{133}$Cs using relativistic coupled-cluster theory. Recently, Roberts and Ginges raised concerns about a part of this calculation that they disagreed with, but in an accompanying calculation, we show that we addressed this issue within our approach, and that it is also consistent with calculations done using a different method, with very small differences, less than 0.1 percent, which are negligible compared to experimental and other theoretical uncertainties. Therefore, our result remains consistent with other physics findings, as reported in a 2019 paper.

A twist is essentially an element of the braid group $PGL_{n+1}(\mathbb{Z})$, 
which is a subgroup of the mapping class group $S_n$. This twist can be thought of 
as an orientation-preserving 2D crystallographic symmetry operation that involves 
a combination of isometries and a twisting motion along a chosen axis of infinity. 

In this context, we have made significant contributions towards classifying all 
twists within $PGL_{n+1}(\mathbb{Z})$. Our work involves providing explicit descriptions 
of these twists and their centralizers, which is particularly relevant to the 
study of the Morita-Kawai classes for isometries in $PGL_{n}(\mathbb{Z})$. 

Overall, our classification has far-reaching implications in algebraic geometry, 
where it aids in understanding the structure of torus equivelar manifolds with 
crystallographic holonomy, which in turn relates to the study of gauge theories.

Pomona College's Mathematics & Statistics Department has been dedicated to
establishing an inclusive and welcoming environment for all students to
engage in mathematical study. In response to low diversity among majors, the
department initially attempted to address this through targeted programs aimed
at enhancing students' mathematical abilities. Conversely, recent efforts have
shifted to an anti-deficit strategy, which prioritizes creating a inclusive
departmental culture over fixing perceived student deficiencies. Our
department's experiences illustrate the importance of creating a supportive
and inclusive departmental culture in creating a diverse student body.

We examine the boundedness of the fractional series operator $T_{\gamma}$, with its given function form $(T_{\gamma}b)(j)$, in the context of $H^{p}(\mathbb{Z})$ to $\ell^{q}(\mathbb{Z})$. Furthermore, a counter-example demonstrates that the operator $T_{\gamma}$ does not yield a bounded mapping from $H^{p}(\mathbb{Z})$ to $H^{q}(\mathbb{Z})$.

This study offers the first empirical evaluation of the influence of auction format integrity on bidding tactics and outcome profitability. Through a controlled lab experiment where human auction participants interacted with either a trustworthy computer or a manipulative computer acting in its own self-interest, the second-price sealed-bid auction was conducted under various conditions. Our data indicate that the presence of an unscrupulous auction opponent leads to significantly lower bids from human bidders compared to when they compete against an honest computer opponent, effectively demonstrating that the auction format's integrity has a substantial impact on bidding behavior and ultimately the value of auction outcomes.

The explanation for one of cosmology's most significant issues, the cosmological constant, by alternative gravity theories has gained increasing interest to this day. To achieve this, the newly proposed Q-gravity theory, one such theory with theoretical validity and consistency by several researchers, is explored in this study. By examining this model within the framework of a Bianchi-I locally rotationally symmetric universe, the authors derive the field equations and demonstrate that this universe model transitions from an isotropic state to a de Sitter space at early times through dimensional analysis and differential equations. Next, the authors analyze the energy conditions to ascertain whether phantom or non-phantom fluid drives the quiescent era of the universe. Finally, the authors evaluate the size of the non-zero, isotropization-related equation of state parameter and compare the predicted values of this parameter to those of conventional cosmology, thereby demonstrating the potential for Q-gravity to replace General Relativity in late-time universe models.

We initiate a study of local defining ideals of Hessenberg varieties, specifically focusing on the non-regular nilpotent cases, and will particularly examine a specific type of non-regular nilpotent case. By developing a geometric form of vertex decomposition for regular nilpotent Hessenberg varieties, we will leverage this method to construct a Gröbner basis of the corresponding local defining ideal, with the basis having minimal degree and consisting of square-free monomials. Furthermore, we will show that this constructed Gröbner basis comprises splitting endomorphisms, drawing on the work done for non-regular nilpotent Hessenberg varieties by Alon and Sturmfels.

Neural Painters, utilizing a GAN-based approach, generate brushstrokes that are assembled into paintings. Despite GANs' superiority in AI-generated art, their training can be exceptionally challenging. To address these difficulties and accelerate Neural Painter training, we employed Transfer Learning, achieving a notable time reduction from days to just hours without compromising visual quality. Our findings are presented in this study.

We tackle the anomalies with the $K$ and $B$ mesons, along with their respective decays into unusual forms of matter, at once by introducing compositeness with extra particles of similar make-up. Introducing the constituent of the compositive fourth generation fermions leads to a matching of the $K$ and $B$ meson anomalies with the right signs. By including off-diagonal masses and chiral anomalies, we can explain this unique combination. Additionally, the introduction of off-diagonal masses among the compositive fermions allows us to simultaneously resolve the anomalies with the $K$ and $B$ mesons and their unusual decays. As a result, we propose a new model with VLK, which can simultaneously address the $K$ and $B$ mesanomalies and their unusual decays. By considering compositive fermions with distinct mass influences, we find that the lower limits on the compositive scale lie within the range of 3.2 to 4.4 TeV. With the introduction of the off-diagonal mass term, we find that the lower limits on the compositive scale lie within the range of 3.2 to 4.3 TeV, depending on particular parameter settings. Moreover, with an additional off-diagonal mass term, we find that the compositive scale's minimum value is approximately 3.9 TeV for any value of $\beta$.

We introduce a new dataset consisting of 1,474 information-seeking questions, which have been answered using 172 scientific research papers across 22 subject areas. Each answer is specifically located within its corresponding paper. These questions require finding and synthesizing specific details from the papers, rather than simply extracting a predefined segment. Our aim in creating this dataset is to supply high-quality data for developing and assessing NLP systems capable of handling more intricate question-answering tasks. Due to the intricate nature of these tasks, we adopted a crowdsource approach for data annotation. Nevertheless, the intrinsic complexity of these tasks poses significant challenges in achieving consistent, high-quality results, which we sought to mitigate by employing two distinct annotation strategies to ensure reliability and reliability of the dataset.

In order to understand fast neutrino flavor instability in core-collapse supernovae, researchers employed the NuBoLE project's three-dimensional simulations. They analyzed a 15 solar mass star collapse using Boltzmann neutrino transport, observing numerous instability characteristics within the protoneutron star. They discovered that regions featuring both electron neutrinos and antineutrinos peak densities and matched energy spectra often exhibit flavor instability. They also noted that regions isolated from the star's center can display instability, while those near it typically exhibit it; however, this does not consistently hold true for all regions. They found that the instability often appears in regions where it is initially triggered by star collapse or protoneutron star cooling, or occasionally, self-sustaining; moreover, it doesn't always produce mixed state flavor fronts, but such fronts typically result in it, often appearing as it propagates through regions of it, whether originally triggered by star collapse or self-sustaining; they discovered that both mixed-state flavor fronts and region-traversing instability can lead to it becoming inhomogeneous, sometimes resulting in it becoming in a in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in in

ADHD is a widely recognized neurodevelopmental disorder that affects children globally, and researchers have found supporting evidence of its existence through neuroimaging, revealing distinct patterns of altered brain function. Effective treatment of ADHD is challenging to achieve, and accessing advanced medical imaging technology is both time-consuming and not feasible for many. To address these challenges, we aim to use machine learning and advanced neuroimaging, which can leverage the value of information with reduced data and time, for diagnosing ADHD. To that end, we employ Deep Learning to pinpoint a subset of crucial brain regions in resting-state fMRI scans of children, using only the essential parts of the brain to train a binary classifier for accurate ADHD diagnosis. Our deep learning framework, designed to identify key brain regions, consists of two main components: an encoder and a decoder. The encoder learns to identify the most informative parts of the brain, and the decoder minimizes information loss by reconstructing the original brain data from the compressed representation. By optimizing both components, we can effectively compress the binary data and select the most critical brain parts. Our study's results indicate that using the essential brain parts can enhance ADHD diagnosis accuracy by approximately 3% compared to using the entire brain, and it can also reduce training time, making diagnosis more efficient and effective.

In a discrete-time epidemic SISI model where population growth is constant and balanced, the per capita mortality and fertility rates are equivalent, and the model's evolution operator is a nonlinear function of seven parameters. When we reduce this operator to a quadratic stochastic one, we show that it has a unique interior fixed point and examine the long-term trajectory behavior under specific conditions regarding the model parameters.

Identifying and understanding the meaning of abbreviations such as 'NASA' is a challenging task for machines, but crucial for applications like identifying the '1998' date or 'DC' as Washington DC versus Detroit. The problem is even more complex with case-sensitive and disambiguation tasks, like 'O' as an O-ring or top, and 'O' as a person's initial. The MadDog system aims to automatically identify and disambiguate acronym instances in texts, utilizing a dictionary of known acronyms and further refining its capabilities with distributional information and argumentation-based disambiguation. The system's capabilities are demonstrated on sample texts and its evaluation through O evaluation and O eval2 protocols shows promising results.

Our research shows that the thermoelectric response of quantum Hall junctions can be manipulated by adding interference patterns through carefully designed splitter and combiner structures near the edges of the material. In particular, our calculations indicate that at specific values of magnetic field, the thermoelectric response of multiple QH junctions experiences sudden changes in spin and valley dependent ways due to interference effects, while the average thermal energy flow passes through these junctions in one direction only when the magnetic field value is not an integer multiple of the base unit.

Our proposed DNA-storage system includes two innovative contributions to its architecture: first, a hierarchical file organization within the DNA, enabling direct access to specific files without the need for extensive decoding and error correction; second, a dynamic data-update mechanism that allows targeted modifications to individual DNA tubes and flexible update strategies to optimize decoding and update costs. These hierarchical and update structures are supported by new techniques that enable access to specific DNA strands and manageable data updates. Our experimental evaluation demonstrates the practical feasibility and performance benefits of these contributions in terms of decoding and update efficiency.

Topological insulators represent a significant phenomenon in modern condensed matter research, with one particularly fascinating feature being the appearance of robust, gapless one-dimensional conductive paths within a non-conductive material's momentum space, known as nodal lines. These lines can be seen as a result of a change in the system's topological characteristics, often marked by a specific value of a parameter called the 3D Torus topological invariant. Thanks to their unique properties, nodal lines have been observed in various systems, such as certain metals and a class of semi-conductors called Weyl metals, as well as in engineered photonic and phononic crystals. This brief overview will explore the theoretical underpinnings of topological invariants, as well as the formation of nodal lines and their resulting surface states in momentum space, with a focus on recent discoveries in photonic and other artificial systems where such nodal lines have been intentionally created and manipulated.

In regenerative tissues such as the heart and brain, cells called pacemakers initiate and control the rhythm of self-sustaining wavefronts that drive processes like cardiac activity. The theoretical properties of these waves, specifically their speed and amplitude, can be experimentally measured. The objective of this study is to use various mathematical models to approximate the properties of pacemaker-driven waves in two dimensions. The findings in this study align with existing research but also uncover new analytical methods to property wave amplitude and velocity in complex systems.

A fundamental concept, entropy, has significant implications in both quantum and classical probability theory, however computing it in classical systems is known to be computationally intensive, specifically P#-complete. In quantum systems, measuring the entropy of unknown states is shown to be at least as hard as the PP^NP-complete problem. In contrast to previous results that required precise entropy calculation, our research presents methods for quantum systems that estimate entropy to constant factors in sublinear time. Furthermore, for classical systems, we establish algorithms operating in BQP^NP that estimate entropy within a polynomial term. Both of our algorithms function efficiently even when dealing with quantum systems containing an exponentially large number of qubits. In quantum systems, our method utilizes the quantum counting technique. As for classical systems, we introduce a modified version of the quantum sampling algorithm by Valiant and also use the quantum counting technique.

Implementing and deploying effective AI/ML solutions necessitates adherence to technical constraints across three key areas: efficient data management, astute cloud utilization, and optimized AI pipeline construction. This implementation should also respect basic technical regulations, including those related to security and compliance. Our comprehensive report provides technical guidance and recommendations to assist engineers and data scientists in making informed decisions that enhance the performance and scalability of their AI/ML models through optimized data storage, astute cloud utilization, and streamlined AI pipeline development. The document also highlights critical security and compliance guidelines to ensure the integrity and legitimacy of AI/ML implementations.

Effective diagnosis coding in healthcare is crucial for analyzing clinical data and measuring hospital performance. Despite the benefits it brings, accurately coding diagnoses can be a costly and time-consuming process due to the technical language doctors use in their notes. To address this issue, machine learning techniques have been developed to bridge the communication gap between clinicians and administrators by converting clinical notes into diagnostic codes. We examine the feasibility of using semi-self-supervised learning methods to automatically identify ICD-10 diagnoses from unstructured clinical notes without requiring extensive manual annotations. Our approach employs the ICD-10 diagnosis codes themselves to train a model using k-means, which is then used in conjunction with a BERT-based clinical text encoder. Our experiments reveal that the semi-self-supervised method achieves comparable, and in some cases superior, performance to a fully-supervised approach, with a 4-fold cross-validation F1-score of 0.8013 for the entire dataset and a significant 0.04 improvement in F1-score for specific patient cases with substantial clinical findings.

Let $R$ be a polynomial ring in $n$ variables over a field $k$. A monomial ideal $I$ within this ring is considered. This paper explores almost Cohen-Macaulay simplicial complexes and provides specific classifications for certain types of ideals, including polymatroidal Veronese type and transversal polymatroidal ideals, along with illustrative examples.

This study presents quantum machine learning approaches for unsupervised and supervised learning tasks on superconducting qubit-based quantum processors. A specific circuit model is used to implement a variational quantum eigensolver-based algorithm for dimensionality reduction and a variational quantum eigensolver-based kernel machine algorithm for classification and regression tasks. These processes are optimized using the classical gradient descent algorithm. The circuits were successfully built using 4 and 8 qubits for these tasks respectively, with quantum data input for all cases. The results obtained match well with classical expectations and show that quantum processors can be utilized for machine learning tasks using superconducting qubits.

Our latest analysis of nearly 170 million stars from the 2018 observations by the Korean Microlens Terrestrial Planet Scan, led to the discovery of 11 new exoplanets and a systematic search for more such planets in similar systems across 44 fields. Ultimately, we monitored a total of 1,056 prime-field areas for approximately 100 nights, resulting in a total sample of 14 million stars. By applying the same detection method that previously yielded numerous planet discoveries, we were able to detect a total of 11 exoplanets in eleven prime-field areas. Our work provides a comprehensive dataset of 11 exoplanets discovered through this method, and also reveals a systematic search for more such planets in similar systems across 38 prime-field areas for approximately 67 million stars.

Differentiable rendering has gained significant traction in solving inverse problems due to its approach of utilizing rendered shadows and approxiable derivatives of the forward model. However, the accurate calculation of the normal derivative required by the adjoint equation has been challenging, largely due to the difficulties associated with numerical methods and the limitations of the volume rendering algorithm, especially in the context of smooth normal fields and alpha-blending. To address this issue, a novel, efficient technique for computing the normal derivative of the radiance function along the ray is presented. This technique integrates the gradient of the shadow function, which can also derive the derivative of a shadow image given the scene and camera data, thereby enabling the application in various inverse problems such as volumetric shape from silhouette and occlusion tomography. To validate the effectiveness of this technique, the paper provides the derivation of the adjoint operator and implements it in occlusion tomography, achieving accurate and rapid results with minimal memory consumption. Furthermore, the implementation exhibits no numerical instability or errors in the gradient calculation.

Recent research has shown the value of probabilistic modeling for traffic demand estimation. Building on this concept, an innovative approach is presented to estimate an origin-destination demand matrix based on traffic observations- specifically volume and occupancy data collected at various links and sensors. This model incorporates statistical noise and originates from the principle of maximum entropy, incorporating expectations on traffic flow on specified origins-destinations and link demand on observed traffic data. The resulting probabilistic model allows for the calculation of an optimal traffic assignment, incorporating statistical noise, along with confidence intervals for key metrics, such as travel time, route selection probability, and travel time reliability, including minimum, mean, and 95th percentile. The effectiveness of this model is demonstrated through a case study using synthetic data based on traffic patterns in the Atlanta area.

In an array of nonlinear oscillators with random frequencies and purely conserved interactions, global phase coherence is demonstrated to occur within finite networks and further examined as it collapses through the generation of localized periodic and chaotic waves following a parameter adjustment. For weak nonlinearity in the system, these global phases exhibit a temporary state of stability, akin to that observed in nearly conservative systems. The obtained results are also compared to the outcome of a simplified phase model where the oscillations' amplitudes are eliminated under an adiabatic process.

The well-documented Aldous-Broder and Wilson algorithms create random spanning trees through random walks, and this research examines their synergy in a single process. Ando et al.'s two-stage tree-construction methods are related to these algorithms, and we demonstrate the possibility of generating a uniform spanning tree in two steps by combining these algorithms for all vertices in the graph in one operation. A specific example is given to show that a spanning tree is not guaranteed to be uniform if the first root choice has an uneven distribution. Our work also examines root placement on the spanning tree's edges and offers a novel approach to generate uniform spanning trees using random edge samplings.

This work presents a novel music dataset named MusicTM-Dataset that comprises sheet music, corresponding lyrics, and audio files. The dataset is designed to foster research on multimodal representation learning, combining visual, textual, and auditory modalities. Visually, the sheet music is treated as an image while being analyzed structurally, modally, and content-wise. The current MusicTM-Dataset includes three subsets: VCVC-100, VCVC-300, and VCVC-500, covering three speeches by VCVC with 100, 300, and 500 measures respectively. We also introduce a baseline network that integrates a CNN with joint attention and a multi-layer percection for fusing sheet music, lyrics, and audio features. The sheet music features are generated through optical character recognition (OCR), which is shown to contribute beneficial information despite its potential to introduce noise. Experimental results on VCVC-100, VCVC-300, and VCTM-500 subsets reveal that the sheet music generated via OCR can yield improved performance in multiple tasks, such as musical backtracking and speech content prediction. We plan to release the MusicTM-Dataset along with the baseline code upon publication.

One major obstacle when utilizing Linked Data lies in developing intuitive and user-friendly interfaces accessible to individuals who aren't technologically inclined. To address this, Ontodia enables the creation of intuitive visual interfaces for Linked Data by creating semantic networks and allowing the incorporation of technical annotations and custom labels. To enhance the exploration of large datasets like Wikidata, we employed clustering and applied Daniel Klein's Nearest Neighbor algorithm, incorporating pre-trained word embeddings from ClusAlgo and AlSnoopy. We tested our approach with diverse queries against the Wikidata dataset, showcasing its effectiveness in grouping and labeling visual nodes within an Ontodia interface, especially when utilizing Daniel Klein's technical optimization to speed up exploration and enable instant node labeling.

We've discovered that in the nonlinear Schr\"{o}dinger equation with variable refractive index and a cubic optical Kerr nonlinearity, solitons with a flat-top profile emerge when the condition for mirror reflection meets these nonlinear effects. The characteristics of resulting dark solitons are explored by examining their behavior in a model with a parabolic nonlinearity index.

This study examines the concept of providing direct assistance in visual analytics tasks, including tasks where algorithms take initiative and users accept guidance willingly. To clarify this concept, we present a model outlining the requirements for a system that offers guided support, along with an exploration of potential applications for this approach. We also delve into the technical hurdles that need to be addressed to realize guided visual analytics systems and discuss two prototypes – Lotse and SHARKIE – that demonstrateassistive capabilities. Finally, we suggest a research agenda for further investigation into providing guidance in various contexts.

We've developed an innovative approach for designing stellarators with considerable versatility. Flexibility in these devices is crucial for achieving optimal plasma performance using this type of magnetic confinement system. Our method is based on an enhanced stellarator coil optimization framework, incorporating additional flexibility in plane selection, p-modes, and error tolerance based on various plasma equilibria. These equilibria represent different rotational transform values determined by plasma pressure profiles from multiple discharge scenarios. We illustrate the effectiveness of this approach with newly optimized LHD-style and W7-style coils, featuring enhanced flexibility compared to existing designs, in both a six-coil and tail-coil configuration. Our innovative system allows for the rapid generation of optimized coil configurations given the equilibrium data and geometry of module locations, facilitating flexible coil optimization for any new equilibrium within the device's parameter space. This capability could potentially enable real-time flexibility for operating stellarators.

Achieving uniform temperature distribution in fixed beds is crucial for optimal performance of catalytic reactions and heat transfer operations. However, obtaining precise temperature measurements within porous particle beds is difficult due to their small scale and the interference of reactive gases and catalysts with common sensing methods. Our approach utilizes T1 temperature-dependent magnetic resonance imaging to non-invasively obtain three-dimensional temperature maps of a gas-solid fixed bed at a resolution of 300 micrometers and a rate of 3 seconds per scan. These measurements demonstrate the impact of gas flow rate and bed porosity on temperature distribution, and we develop a dimensionless correlation to describe the average temperature increase across the bed based on these factors.

Within a cell, proteins and nucleic acids form membraneless droplets, known as biomolecular condensates, through liquid-like phase separation. These droplets play a role in generating functional compartments, but the interactions between components of different droplets have yet to be fully understood. To gain insight into this area, a new framework is introduced to study the phase separation of a cell-like mixture, comprised of different types of molecules, some of which bind in pairs but others don't. Through the application of key principles and the development of an equation to describe this mixture, conditions are established for the emergence of multiple phases and the quantitative analysis of their boundaries is then conducted using an advanced numerical method. The results of this study show that when multiple droplet types coexist with free unbound components, their concentrations on the boundaries are related to a fundamental mathematical expression. Additionally, a two-component model system is used to further analyze this phenomenon and the effects of varying concentrations of unbound components are found to significantly impact the boundaries between phases. These findings suggest that future experiments could utilize measurements of unbound components to differentiate between competing theories about droplet formation and the results of this study may also provide a framework for understanding the interactions between condensates formed by different molecules in cellular environments.

Using the Helioseismic and Magnetic Imager on the Solar Dynamics Observatory, we studied how a major leading sunspot rotated in NOAA AR 11429 during two powerful solar flares. A notable sunspot rotated in an unconventional direction, influenced significantly by the solar eruptions. Moving disturbances within other sunspots, caused by the solar flares, traveled at high speeds and were detected using the helioseismic method as wave propagation. The disturbances, possibly related to jet-like flows or magnetosonic waves, emerged from the leading sunspot and moved across the sunspot group, affecting other sunspots in the group. A second high-speed feature appeared in the following day's observations, suggesting the presence of multiple jet events. This study suggests that the solar flares induced the high-speed flows through the distortion of the sunspot's magnetic field, a process supported by the observed changes in the sunspot's magnetic field using vector magnetograms.

This note presents a new category of map functions known as oriented colored broken submersions, which forms the most basic level of a complex structure. It is demonstrated that every closed manifold possesses at least one map that doesn't vanish, when colored with this specific type of broken submersions, which in turn implies the initial version of the Mumford Conjecture, also known as the Massey partial connectivity hypothesis for manifolds.

This research paper conducts a comprehensive comparison of various multilevel preconditioners for solving cardiac mechanics problems, using the FEniCS platform and a finite element method. A hierarchical spectral element method is employed to create fast solvers capable of handling large and detailed 3D models efficiently. The investigation involves three key algorithms for initial vector approximation and a set of three techniques for solving linear systems at the core of each algorithm. The research demonstrates the fast convergence and low computational cost of ARMS and SMG for solving cardiac mechanics problems, making these methods suitable for large-scale and highly detailed models. Moreover, a fast empty domain fill-in smoothing algorithm is proposed, which outperforms existing techniques in terms of speed, memory usage, and convergence rate. The research also explores the application of these preconditioners on high-performance computing systems, achieving a notable speedup of speedup > 5 for our SMG variant.

The analysis of a temporal, distributed system like Flickr's tag cloud is a complex task, and several approaches have been taken to understand its behavior. This paper applies system thinking and interest propagation theories to model Flickr's tag cloud, considering both user-initiated and automatic (from page titles) tag creation. Tag use is seen as a form of temporary resource that can be shared, and collaborative tag development is modeled as a process of temporary and permanent connections between tags, leading to the emergence of distinct communities of interest. The results support this modeling methodology and provide insights into Flickr's community structure and behavior, and similar understanding can be achieved for other social tagging systems.

Recently, there has been significant interest in acoustic metamaterials, which are designed using sub-wavelength units to control sound waves across various frequencies and applications, such as sensors and ultrasonic imaging. Acoustic metasurfaces, which are thin layers of these units, are particularly effective at high frequencies, allowing for compact and efficient acoustic wave manipulation. This study presents a novel, compact and highly sensitive ultrasonic detector that functions in the 20-100 MHz frequency range and is based on integrated acoustic micro-metagratings, which are fabricated using two-photon polymerization (TPP). By using computer-generated structures, the researchers were able to achieve high sensitivity to ultrasonic waves at specific frequencies, such as 30 MHz and 100 MHz. Acoustic simulations confirmed that the acoustic radiation pressure exerted by these metagratings can be concentrated into highly pressurized regions, which can be detected by integrated piezoelectric layers. This technology holds promise for integrating acoustic micro-metagratings with electronic systems, potentially leading to integrated, compact and highly sensitive micro-acoustic devices.

This paper primarily focuses on the long-term behavior of strong solutions to the two-dimensional compressible FENE dumbbell model. Utilizing the Fourier splitting technique, we demonstrate that the $L^2$ decay rate is given by $\ln^{-l}(e+t)$ with any positive integer $l$, which is consistent with the results of recent studies (you can find them in the references provided below: [8-10], [13-17], [19-24]). By employing the time-weighted energy method, we establish sub-exponential decay rates and, in the process, overcome the common dissipation mechanism limitation.

The mobile internet's explosive growth has spurred the need to expand and optimize its capabilities, especially in areas experiencing congestion. To address this demand, 3GPP introduced the Integrated Access and Backhaul (IAB) as a means of streamlining wireless backhaul implementation and reducing network deployment costs. To further meet mobile users' needs, 3GPP is now exploring the possibility of deploying IAB in mobile user equipment. This concept, known as Mobile IAB, has the potential to transform mobile computing and revolutionize various applications, especially those requiring low latency, such as virtual reality and telemedicine. This paper provides an in-depth analysis of Mobile IAB's underlying problems, potential uses cases, and associated challenges, and proposes a comprehensive taxonomy to guide its implementation and deployment.

In this study, we conduct an extensive examination of five leading global optimization algorithms as a hyperparameter configuration problem to understand the overall impact of their settings on performance. By utilizing three methods of sensitivity analysis and evaluating various adjustable parameters, such as covariance matrix adaptation, differential evolution, and non-dominated sorting, we analyze their behavior when influenced by different factors. The results, processed through an automated framework, reveal the overall importance of each algorithm's settings, revealing significant differences in the overall effect of different parameters, such as mutation and exploration strategies, across all methods and reproducible runs. The ranking of parameters, such as \boldmath{\sigma} and F, varies significantly, however, depending on the sensitivity analysis method used, highlighting different degrees of interaction and varying numbers of evaluated and penalized factors. The findings also show significant variation in the effect of different parameters, such as \boldmath{p}_m and F, across multiple independent, representative, and parallelized algorithm executions, underscoring the need for a more in-depth and in-depth analysis of the overall sensitivity and interaction of the algorithm's settings.

The paper addresses misconceptions surrounding Jefimenko's equations, which are derived from Maxwell's equations, for a specific charge and current configuration obeying the continuity equation. It then compares the time evolution of this charge and current setup with that of the wave equation, demonstrating that the two descriptions yield identical results. As a consequence, the paper concludes that the use of potentials in such a configuration is gauge invariant for any gauge, including those involving Heaviside and retarded potentials. Furthermore, the paper draws parallels between these findings in quantum electrodynamics and the principles of path integration. Ultimately, the paper suggests a fundamental equivalence between QED and a theoretical framework devoid of potentials, thereby supporting the notion that potentials are unphysical in quantum theory.

Despite notable advancements in reinforcement learning, particularly within well-defined benchmarks, these methods often fail to generalize to more complex tasks and environments. To investigate this issue, multiple research groups have explored continual and lifelong learning, aiming to develop models capable of adapting to new, unseen environments without resetting. However, evaluating progress in this area remains challenging due to the absence of standardized procedures. To address this gap, we introduce L2Explorer, a comprehensive Python package that provides a wide range of diverse and complex exploration environments. Additionally, the package includes thorough evaluation protocols to facilitate robust comparison of different strategies. By offering a robust platform for action, we hope to stimulate further research and development in creative methods for environmental exploration and procedure design. The L2Explorer package is available for download at: https://github.com/justin2explorer/L2Explorer

Liger, a next-generation infrared device at the W. M. Keck Observatory, features a customized data processing system to analyze observed data. Developed by ConsenSys and Caltech, this system utilizes the ESO Science Data Management System framework by designing data processing modules, observation control interfaces, and a calibration data insertion system. The observation control system is divided into two components: a system with direct telescope access and a system used by scientists at their workstations, which communicate via TCP/IP. The Liger data reduction system is now fully integrated into the Keck Scientific Operations Data Reduction System.
This study uncovers a broad class of non-trivial and smooth traveling wave solutions for the 2D Euler equation in the vicinity of the Couette flow.

We experimentally control the linear polarization of exciton-polariton condensates using optical traps with elliptical geometries that favor specific polarization modes. Due to anisotropic splitting in the cavity, ground state degeneracy is lifted, yielding fine structure modes along the trap's axis and orthogonal to it. These modes are selectively occupied by the condensate. Our results reveal a unique method for polarization control with potential applications in spin-based photonics and research on complex optical systems with adjustable coupling properties.

This study is set within deterministic stochastic PDE theory, with particular emphasis on the KPZ equation and related equations. The authors derive stochastic equations of this type by deriving statistical measures, such as correlation functions and space-time averages, from regular, symmetric, interacting particle systems known as Gibbs fields. These measures stem from regular KPZ-type equations that include nonlocal 'gradient terms' and are derived using variational formulas and a combination of techniques such as duality and space-time variational formulas. The resulting operations and equations are linked to concepts of Hamilton-Jacobi theory and Hamiltonian systems, while converging to nonlocal variational formulas that drive the limit turbulent states and turbulence-like phenomena in low-dimensional turbulent flows. The limiting turbulent states are identified as equilibrium states of associated nonlocal Hamiltonian systems and are shown to exhibit nontrivial dynamics and complex behavior. The space-time variational formulas that result are demonstrated to converge to converging space-time variational formulas that drive turbulent phenomena in low-dimensional variational theories, with phenomena such as solitons, soliton trains, wave turbulence, and wave turbulence with turbulent states. The concepts and equations that result are shown to have a broader connection to concepts and equations that govern turbulent flows and nonlinear waves.

The emergence of the novel coronavirus in December 2019 in Wuhan, China, led to a global pandemic that overwhelmed healthcare systems and caused over a million deaths within a year. To combat this crisis, countries around the world implemented various measures, such as lockdowns, to slow down the virus's spread. In response to the COVID-19 outbreak, South Africa introduced its first lockdown on the 26th of March 2020, following the infection of over a thousand people. To manage the crisis, the government announced the closure of schools and businesses, enforced social distancing, and shut down borders. To gain a better understanding of the virus's spread, the government launched the SARS-CoV-2 National Contact Tracing System. To further analyze the virus's spread, researchers in South Africa launched the COVID-19 SA Dashboard. To provide real-time information on the virus's spread, the government announced the closure of schools and businesses, implemented social distancing, and shut down borders.

Freiman's 3k-4 theorem, an fundamental result in additive combinatorics, can be restated as follows: given a set of n integers from 1 to m, where the sum of any two elements does not exceed m, the size of the set combined with its additive inverse is at least 2n, and at most O(n), and if these conditions are met, the set is a subset of a arithmetic progression with a size of O(n), which in turn implies that the set is a subset of a set of n integers from 1 to m, that combined with an additive inverse forms a set of n integers from 1 to m, that combined with an additive inverse forms a set of n integers from 1 to m, that combined with an additive inverse forms a set of n integers from 1 to m.

In this work, the author presents a refined version of Freiman's 3k-4 theorem, with the following improvement: the set of n integers from 1 to m, that combined with an additive inverse forms a set of n integers from 1 to m, that combined with an additive inverse forms a set of n integers from 1 to m, that combined with an additive inverse forms a set of n integers from 1 to M, that combined with an additive inverse forms a set of n integers from 1 to M, that combined with an additive inverse forms a set of n integers from 1 to M,

Recent advancements in deep learning have led to the success of using it in medical image classification tasks. In this research, a novel multimodal information fusion approach is proposed to enhance automatic disease classification in OCT B-Scan and DR in fundus images. OCT B-Scan images were used in the initial experiment, where the proposed method achieved a superior classification performance of 0.989 AUC on two different datasets. Subsequently, an extended approach was devised to address the distinct characteristics of OCT B-Scan and fundus images. This approach initially involves extracting sub-modal information using multiple sub-CNNs, followed by a first fusion of their outputs using a random forest. Finally, the modalities are combined through another CNN to refine the sub-modal representations and generate a unified feature set for classification. This approach has demonstrated a superior classification performance of 0.985 AUC and 0.982 AUC on two datasets, respectively, for OCT B-Scan and fundus images.

X-ray images contain subtle characteristics that can aid in predicting the severity of COVID-19 patients and the likelihood of ICU admission. To identify these features, we employed machine learning to analyze and compare X-ray images of patients based on their outcome (ICU admission or not). Our method involved creating XOR networks, which categorize X-ray images into two classes and reject input that doesn't fit well. By distributing these models into two groups (potential yes/no answers), we used the intersection of their outputs as an indicator for COVID-19 severity. This indicator was then used to categorize the remaining patients into potential ICU admission cases. Our study used 1,102 X-ray images of patients diagnosed with COVID-19, and our findings revealed an X-ray characteristic that can predict ICU admission with around 70% accuracy.

This study focuses on one-dimensional spherically stratified media, examining the transmission eigenfunctions and their related transmission eigenvalues within this framework. Mathematical analysis demonstrates that as energy increases, absolute values of the transmission eigenfunctions and their associated transmission eigenvalues exhibit similar trends. It is proven that the absolute values of the transmission eigenfunctions are strictly localized at both boundaries of such media, with their values at these boundaries可直接 used to derive a novel and useful Goos-Hänkel-like formula applicable to 1-D perfectly conducting spherical metallic particles.

To expand a dialogue system's capabilities and handle an ever-growing variety of user needs, users can express their desires in multiple ways, making it difficult for basic dialogue systems to accurately identify new intent categories without extensive annotated data our proposed framework addresses this challenge by leveraging a language model's ability to capture consistent intent patterns and utilizing a labeled dataset to guide its pre-training. Furthermore, we utilize an unlabeled dataset to enhance generalization and employ contrastive learning to streamline discovery and minimize dependency on annotated examples. As a result, our approach significantly improves overall accuracy, exact match rates on labeled tasks, and achieves nearly double the accuracy on unsupervised tasks when evaluated on a unified platform for dialogue intent discovery.

The classical universal bundle functor W mapping from the category of simplicial groups in C to the category of simplicial sets in C lifts to a monadic structure on the category of simplicial groups in C, and this extension holds for simplicial algebras defined by any Lawvere theory that includes group theory.
In our analysis, we demonstrate that a finite group of order $r$ possesses no more than $$7.3722\cdot r^{\frac{\log_2r}{4}+1.5315}$$ subgroups.

This study re-examines the Adler-Bobenko-Suris H2 equation. The equation is shown to be derivable through the nonlocal derivative of the common spatial derivative. Additionally, a distinct nonlocal derivative form is found for the H2 equation, placing it in a derivative of a gradient map with a higher order, specifically of a 4th order. The study also explores the compatibility of the derivative map with the Miura map, used to link the KdV and the HDKV equation. It finds that the Miura map commutes with the 4th order derivative map, leading to a new, simplified form for the derivative map on the derivative of the KdV equation, and thus a new expression for the nonlocal derivative map on the derivative of the HDKV equation.

This paper delves into the source of high false positive rates in Visual Relationship Detection (VRD). During training, VRD models frequently fail to attribute attributes to unrelated objects, resulting in a discrepancy between predicted attributes and object-attribute relationships that hampers their ability to overcome false positives in Visual Grounding (VG). To address this problem, we introduce a new layer to the VRD framework that focuses on Visual Relationship Verification (VRV). By taking the attributes predicted by the leading VRD approaches as a starting point, VRV thoroughly examines each visual relationship to filter out incorrect predictions and their corresponding predicted locations. As a result, the proposed method effectively mitigates false positives in VRD and enhances prediction accuracy in tasks involving multiple Visual Relationships and objects with similar appearances. Our approach achieves a substantial 21.1% improvement in VRD mAP when applied to the COCO-KP dataset and demonstrates robust generalization capabilities across multiple datasets with a robust cross-task ability to address Visual Grounding problems.

A new measure, referred to as quantum correlation cost (QCC), quantifies the amount of quantum correlation employed in weak measurement procedures based on the principle of state update reduction. It serves as the dual of relative entropy of independence and can be expressed through a formula involving the relative entropy of QCC of a bipartite quantum state and its corresponding marginal subsystem. It has been demonstrated that the QCC achieves a minimum value when bipartite quantum states exhibit maximal quantum correlation. A further investigation into the QCC of specific bipartite quantum states such as isotropic and Werner states was also undertaken.

Artificial intelligence systems capable of modeling complex social relationships are referred to as social relationship graph generation tasks. Existing approaches typically combine multiple algorithms to achieve a satisfactory result. In this research, a unified neural network model is developed to automatically generate a complex social graph based on a given set of individual characteristics. The proposed method leverages learned representations of traits and dynamically created relationships between sample pairs to predict accurate connections. Furthermore, it enables the prediction of group memberships within a network. Empirical tests were conducted on two publicly available social datasets, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed approach in generating accurate social graphs. Additionally, generation quality is enhanced by incorporating an generative adversarial network that utilizes a sample-based goal function to guide the creation process.

Capturing long-range relationships in scene understanding tasks is crucial for achieving a comprehensive comprehension of image content. Attention networks excel in modeling dynamic, context-sensitive relationships but are inefficient due to their $O(N^2)$ complexity, making them impractical for images with a large number of pixels ($N$). In an effort to reduce this complexity, we propose the dynamic graph message passing network (DGMPN), which operates on pixel grids and facilitates efficient long-range interaction. By passing messages only between locally connected pixels via a graph's adjacency matrix, DGMPN restricts the attention to $O(N)$ and still achieves comparable results to attention models. We validate the efficacy of DGMPN across multiple scene understanding tasks, including semantic segmentation, domain-adaptive segmentation, and spatial relationship prediction, demonstrating its superior performance and enhanced training efficiency.

Optimizing hardware efficiency in digital circuits often involves a common operation known as multiple constant multiplication (MCM). Our research focuses on developing an innovative approach to perform MCm with minimal hardware cost. Our innovative algorithm identifies and groups compatible and adjacent coefficients, which are then replaced by a single equivalent multiplication operation using a compatible and adjacent multiple constant multiplication (CAMCM) equivalent. Following this replacement, the remaining multiplication operations are optimized using an existing optimization method, specifically the unrolled high-radix Schanuel method (UHR-Sch). Our approach is evaluated using the technology mapping method using the open source ABC tool on ISCAS-89 benchmark circuits. Our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm significantly reduces the hardware cost (area and power) while increasing the maximum operating frequency by up to 14%, compared to the state-of-the-art method UHR-Sch.

The intersection of quantum computing and deep neural networks has recently given rise to a growing research field, known as quantum deep learning. Despite previously being separate entities, advancements in quantum computing and high-performance distributed systems have enabled the convergence of these domains. This has led to the development of novel opportunities and also a set of challenges. In contrast to widespread knowledge about classical deep learning, there is less documentation available about quantum deep learning and its associated hurdles. This article aims to bridge that knowledge gap by offering a comprehensive overview of quantum deep learning, along with insights into the quantum hardware and software infrastructure, as well as the specific challenges and benefits it presents. It also explores the primary applications of quantum deep learning and provides directions for future research in the field.

The radio frequency (RF) accelerator technology is the backbone of modern particle accelerators, playing a crucial role in determining its maximum luminosity and intensity. This frequency-based system also influences the energy-range and beam emittance of the accelerators. Given its significance, continuous research and development in RF technology is essential for advancing existing and emerging RF accelerator programs. This could potentially lead to innovative solutions and applications beyond its current uses. This "report from the future" provides an overview of current RF accelerator operations, recent research and development efforts, and emerging technologies, including superconducting, room-temperature accelerating structures, particle-in-cell simulations, and cathode development. It also discusses non-linear beam dynamics and advanced beam diagnostics needed to enhance the luminosity and emittance of the accelerators.

In the near future, physicists anticipate that the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) will discover new physics. However, the specific characteristics and energy thresholds of this new physics remain unknown. To gain a clearer understanding, a transition to a precise measurement regime is necessary. Lepton colliders, such as the muon-muon collider, offer distinct advantages due to their unique production method, making them ideal for this type of research. This review outlines the progress made in the LHC's data analysis and the subsequent research progress at the muon collider facility, as well as the challenges and planned research directions that could contribute significantly to the new physics research program.

We have determined the dispersion relations for relativistic fluid modes in various configurations - longitudinal, transverse, and spin-related - and found that these differ between a viscosity type that skews in one direction and a viscosity that is symmetric in its impact. Additionally, our analysis shows that the temperature and mean free path determine if the modes are damped or enhanced in their movement.

Our research assesses whether the cosmic background of Hawking radiation from primordial black holes could be detected as an excess in the CMB, radio waves, or both. CMB experiments have already set the CMB excess limit at a level of $10^{-29}$ eV cm$^2$ s, which translates to a limit of $M_{\rm PBH} \lesssim 3 \times 10^{23}$ kg for the mass of the black holes. For a wide range of CMB experiments with varying sensitivities, the PBH mass range is determined to be between $10^{21}$ kg and $10^{24}$ kg. For the case where only the radio excess is considered, the limits on the decay rate of the black holes lead to a PBH mass range of between $10^{20}$ kg and $10^{23}$ kg. These findings suggest that the development of more sensitive CMB and radio frequency telescopes could enable the detection of the Hawking radiation of the primordial black holes, which could confirm quantum gravity effects within the range of general relativity.

Introducing the Virtual Secure Platform (VSP), a pioneering solution that brings together cryptography and processing power in a single apparatus, allowing multiple confidential users to collaborate on complex computational tasks.
