Accurate categorization of IoT devices is crucial for implementing effective
security measures. Research has demonstrated the benefits of using
characteristic device data, such as those transmitted during Web Proxy
Intermediary (WPITOP) feature sets, to identify IoT devices and block malicious
devices at a network gateway. Yet, transmitting all features can be costly in
terms of energy and bandwidth, particularly for large networks or when using
mobile networks, increasing the risk of exposing private user data. To mitigate
these issues, this study proposes a cost model to evaluate feature extraction
costs based on information theory and mutual information. WPITOP feature
candidates are then ranked according to their utility using the rank and score
intrinsic selection methods. The proposed cost-aware approach is shown to
efficiently select the most relevant features and outperform state-of-the-art
techniques in terms of accuracy and extraction cost.

Godel modal logics can be regarded as an extension of intutionistic modal logics with prelinearity. This study Godel modal logics with the D axiom specifically. The relational semantics for Godel modal logics has been proposed, along with the identification of the algebraic semantics for various sublogics of the D axiom principle. These logics include the Glivenko closure of nilpotent minimal valuations, the logic with variable depth, and the finitely valued logics. In addition, we prove that the algebraic semantics for finitely valued logics coincides with the conservative extension of intutionistic logics with the Chapman axioms, and that the algebraic semantics for the logic with variable depth is a superlattice type algebra with a specific property in its relational frame.

This research presents a novel and straightforward technique for word-alignment that leverages bilingual information from external sources like machine translation and embedding models. The proposed technique surpasses the capabilities of the traditional dynamic time-warping method- the cornerstone of many word-alignment algorithms- by employing a scoring system that evaluates the bilingual information to pinpoint corresponding words. The external bilingual information source is utilized to establish the reference points, whereas machine translation outputs are employed as the reference in some instances. Notably, the new technique does not necessitate the creation of any additional data structures and merely relies on the bilingual information sources' outputs. The evaluation of the technique in various scenarios, including scenarios with and without a reference, demonstrates that the technique is increasingly more efficient as the length disparity between the reference and target sentences grows significantly. Furthermore, the new technique proves to be more efficient than state-of-the-art algorithms such as AligAlign when applied to scenarios with a reference.

We suggest an asynchronous algorithm to solve Nash equilibrium problems by iteratively decomposing the mixed strategies. This methodology is heavily grounded in monotone operator theory, utilizing warped resolvents for handling a combination of nonsmooth and smooth functions involved in strategy mixtures.

The theoretical framework of forming stellar-mass and supermassive black holes within the standard cosmological model is well-established; however, simulating the creation of intermediate-sized black holes within this framework remains challenging, necessitating customized and computationally intensive simulations. In contrast, forming primordial black holes within the standard cosmological model is relatively straightforward to model, allowing for the incorporation of this phenomenon within more comprehensive, population synthesis codes without substantial modifications. A novel simulation module integrated into the PopSyCLE code, which models the formation of primordial black holes based on early universe conditions, is presented. By employing this module, the resulting distribution of black hole masses, including those of primordial black holes, can be efficiently generated. Furthermore, the mass distribution resulting from this simulation module accurately replicates theoretical predictions made by other primordial black hole formation models.

We carried out computer simulations of a system consisting of hard molecular wedges where the angle between the wide and narrow ends significantly affects its properties, and the primary variable is the number of molecules per unit area of its wide section. In the limit of very acute wedge angles, the results are comparable to those from previous studies on hard chain molecules and hard self-attracting wedge-shaped depletions, exhibiting a unique crystal structure with a characteristic "V" shape. For wedge angles of 90 degrees, the results show the occurrence of multiple phases, including a modulated structure with "splay" features and another modulated structure with "herringbone" features, and the findings are discussed considering possible liquid crystal phases with similar characteristics found in systems consisting of molecules with attractive forces.

Recurrences in positive definite functions, particularly concerning the absolute integrability of their Fourier coefficients, were initially explored by I.J. Schoenberg on the real line and later extended to the sphere by D.G. Kendall in 1971. This paper seeks to generalize result (1) to the case of a sphere with radius R, particularly for the case where the order is even and the degree is odd, thus complementing existing knowledge about the matrix Wiener theorem for spherical positive definite functions.

A conventional imaging system relies on detailed measurement of light as it passes through or is reflected off an object and passes through a lens to form an image.  By contrast, our innovative undetected-photon quantum imaging method achieves the same result without the need for any detailed measurements of the photon as it forms an image.  Light with a different wavelength interacts with the object and is then replaced by light of a different wavelength that propagates through free space and then passes through a lens to form an image.  Light is launched into a single-pixel detector and then used to extract correlations between the detector and the image via data analysis.  A proof-of-concept experiment successfully demonstrated the ability to distinguish between an object and its complement in a four-wave mixing setup, and the corresponding quantum data confirmed that this ability is grounded in quantum physics principles.

The flow of complex liquids, such as foams and emulsions, is often hindered by friction as they move through narrow gaps, resulting in significant pressure drops that can impede their transport and even cause damage to their microstructure. Despite recent breakthroughs in understanding the friction of dry foams against solid surfaces, very little is known about the influence of liquid structure on the friction of foams. Through large-scale simulations and experiments, we have established that foam friction in narrow channels is not solely dependent on shear stress but is also significantly affected by the interaction between the liquid and solid surfaces, as well as the resulting liquid menisci that form on the walls. The pressure required to withdraw a liquid meniscus from a solid surface is directly related to the roughness of that surface, and it is this interaction that primarily governs foam friction in narrow gaps. The relationship between the foam's shear stress and the pulling pressure of the meniscus can be used to predict the friction of foams against solid surfaces, and it is also applicable to other multiphase systems where a liquid surrounds a solid within a narrow gap.

This study addresses the challenge in using deep learning for skin cancer detection with datasets that include anomalies, such as mislabeled data and images with skin conditions unrelated to cancer. Although deep learning models excel at processing large datasets quickly, they can struggle with data anomalies, leading to decreased performance on minority classes. To overcome this limitation, the authors propose a novel ensemble approach to identify outlier samples that could adversely affect the deep learning model's performance. By using statistics and entropy-based metrics, the method identifies potential anomalies and removes them before training the deep learning model. The proposed approach was tested on two publicly available skin cancer datasets and demonstrated improved performance, outperforming existing anomaly detection methods by achieving higher accuracy and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve. The code associated with this study is publicly accessible at https://github.com/abdulrahmanmohd/SkinCancerDetection.

We carried out a high-resolution ARPES study on sodium and found that the observed increase in band energy as it approached the Fermi surface could be attributed to enhanced electron-hole interaction. Our measurement of the quasiparticle lifespan within the first parabolic band showed it initially remained constant, but started to decrease as the energy approached the Fermi surface. This finding agrees with calculations that indicate a drop in the density of states at the "Sodium peak" and subsequently a decrease as the doped parabolic band's density of states approaches the Fermi surface. Our research also indicates that using second-order interactions to describe quasiparticle lifetimes near the minimum of the parabolic band may lead to an underestimation of the lifetimes due to the influence of additional scattering processes via interband transitions that become significant as momentum disperses from the minimum.

Building on a novel theory by M. R. L. Maia, this research demonstrates the resolution of the long-standing Lebowitz-Cubo paradox in statistical mechanics. Paradoxical outcomes arise when applying standard methods to compute entropy and the time-dependent Boltzmann distribution in systems exhibiting free expansion or similar behaviors. Standard approaches incorrectly assume a uniform increase in phase space volume with time, leading to false conclusions about entropy growth. In an effort to validate the theory, this paper performs direct calculations of both thermodynamic and kinetic entropy during the free expansion process. Calculations employ both non-relativistic and relativistic $N$-body Hamiltonian trajectories. In all cases, it has been confirmed that the total entropy remains constant, thus validating Maia's claim. To streamline and automate these direct computations, this paper presents a custom-written computer program.

This passage provides an in-depth, explicit calculation for the weights of Kontsevich graphs that emerge from connections and curvatures within a symplectic manifold framework, specifically focusing on globalization. An explicit, detailed formula is given for Kontsevich's $\beta$-weights of 2nd curvature graph $\beta(K)$, that depends on the Euler classes of certain real vector bundles, given by:

$\beta(K)=\int_{\sigma_K}\prod_{i=1}^n\left(\frac{\omega(\vec{v}_i,\vec{u}_i)}{\vec{v}_i\cdot\vec{u}_i}\right)^2.$

We establish a comprehensive formula for $\beta(K)$ by computing how $\beta$ behaves under the B-operator in the symplectic case, leading to the expression:

$I^*(\beta_2(X,Y))=\left[\frac{16\pi^2}{\Gamma(\frac{b}{4})\Gamma(\frac{b+2}{4})}\right]^2\Gamma(\frac{b}{2})\Gamma(\frac{b+1}{2})\pi\cdot\beta_2(Y,X).$

We investigate how nonlinearity affects the woodpile and diatomic chains, particularly in relation to the pure sine Gaussian approximation. This results in modified eigenfunctions that decay exponentially, with two small parameters controlling the rate of decay and forming a pair of symmetric modes known as nanoptera. These modes are characterized by a unique envelope, or "envelope function," whose shape is determined by two key parameters. One parameter, $\gamma$, is derived from the mass and spring constants of the linear system, while the other, $\alpha$, is related to the amplitude of the modes and a period of the grid, making it particularly sensitive to the coupling constants. We analyze the effect of this sensitivity in both the woodpile and diatomic chains models, revealing distinct relationships between the amplitude and coupling constants that define their local "stable" and "unstable" regimes.

Extra energy in certain parts of primordial inflation can leave detectable imprints on both primary cosmic structures and higher-order multipoles generated by inflationary fluctuations. These multipoles are produced by a process of particle-like extraction, facilitated by the expanding universe and its interaction with features of inflation, which also amplify quantum corrections to the scalar spectrum. Lately, researchers have focused on detecting features of primordial inflation using the cosmological collider mechanism, primarily under the assumption that these features arise within the inflaton's quadratic regime. However, if we consider a universe that behaves similarly to the de Sitter space, our analysis shows that even features arising from the inflaton's higher-order processes can be detected through their distinctive exponential decay signatures in the spectra of primordial fluctuations. This substantial energetic extraction results in a classical signal that can be as much as $|\text{Suppressed} / \lambda_{\text{IR}} \times \text{logarithmic factors} |$ times stronger than previously thought possible, where the suppression factor is determined by the difference in mass between the inflaton and the heavier fields interacting with it. These findings demonstrate that even relatively light features can be detected by future precision measurements of primary cosmic structures, and we provide an analytical explanation of this phenomenon based on the exchange of the inflaton with many softer modes.

Consider a graph of even order that is both vertex and edge connected. A "perfect" subgraph can be found within it if every vertex is part of exactly one edge in that subgraph. Our main result shows a large class of Hamiltonian graphs which meet the requirement of a 2-factor and a perfect 3-subgraph, specifically "accordion graphs". Additionally, we demonstrate an optimal set of conditions for a perfect subgraph, and it turns out that an accordion graph contains a perfect subgraph if and only if it also has a perfect 3-factor. Finally, based on an existing result by Li and Wang, we find that the coupon graph, $C_2$, is isomorphic to the catgraph, $CAT_2$, for any even $k \geq 4$.

We carry out a finite-time scaling analysis near the detrapping point in a three-state quantum walk model. The coin operator is adjusted using parameter $\rho$ that controls the speed of wavepacket dispersion. The initial state is a symmetric superposition of two coin operator eigenstates with opposite momenta. One wavepacket travels to the right and one to the left, forming two wavepackets in total. The fraction of particles in the two left-traveling and right-traveling regions is measured. The fractional occupation numbers in these two regions are denoted $P_{\leftarrow}$ and $P_{\rightarrow}$. The values of $P_{\leftarrow}$ and $P_{\rightarrow}$ are measured in the presence of a barrier. The two quantities are found to be equal, $P_{\leftarrow}=P_{\rightarrow}$, for all values of $\rho$. The values of $P_{\leftarrow}$ and $P_{\rightarrow}$ are found to be dependent on $\tau = (\tau_c - \tau)/\tau_c$, where $\tau_c$ is the critical value of $\tau$. The relationship is given by $P_{\leftarrow}=P_{\rightarrow}=|\tau|^{\alpha}$, where $\alpha$ is the critical exponent. The value of $\alpha$ is found to be dependent on $\rho$. The value of $\alpha$ lies between $1$ and $2$ depending on the value of $\

This paper explores the benefits that self-supervised learning confers on Vision Transformers (ViT), distinguishing it from the effects of scale and pre-training, via controlled experiments. We utilized the ImageNet linear probe and the multi-image metric learning head, comparing our results to those from self-supervised Convolutional Networks (ConvNet). Notably, we found that self-supervised ViT exhibits improved performance on semantically challenging, high-frequency, and diverse datasets. Furthermore, we conducted ablation studies to pinpoint the self-supervised learning signals that enable ViT to achieve strong generalization, revealing that ViT with self-supervised learning pre-training exhibits improved robustness to distribution shifts and cleaner feature representations, stemming from its self-supervised capacity for long-range dependency modeling.

A unified dark fluid model has been developed that combines dissipation and a quadratic equation of state to describe the behavior of dark energy and dark matter as a single fluid. This model emerges from applying an Euler-Lagrange equation to a given action. A graph has been created to demonstrate how the fluid's equation of state changes in response to dissipation levels and to a parameter related to the fluid's behavior. Specifically, dissipation is shown to alter the equation of state in a way that depends on a fluid's weight. For a weight of 1/2, dissipation is necessary to maintain stability; otherwise, it leads to an unwanted oscillation in solutions. Model predictions are compared against current observations and demonstrated consistency with a brief cosmological data analysis shows that models with dissipation are more likely than non-dissipative models to be compatible with current data. A 3D visualization is used to illustrate how a model's evolution is influenced by a fluid's weight and by dissipation levels. Furthermore, a data-driven analysis confirms that these models with dissipation are more likely than non-dissipative models.

We present a straightforward proof that in three or more dimensions, the Cauchy problem for the incompressible Euler equations has a critical issue in terms of stability, specifically when using Sobolev spaces and certain types of Lorentz spaces, thereby confirming an earlier study by Bourgain and Li.

Recently, large text-conditioned generative diffusion models have gained significant traction for their ability to generate high-quality images, videos, and audio. In contrast to previous latent diffusion models that rely on image-to-image translation, these new models offer unparalleled flexibility in creating images based on text descriptions and user input. However, this advancement also introduces new challenges in controlling the artistic process and accurately translating text descriptions into visual content. To address these issues, we introduce the Stable Artist, a user-friendly interface that leverages the power of stable diffusion while prioritizing user control and clarity. As stable diffusion generates images in a latent space, our interface utilizes this latent space to empower users and utilize concept towers to establish structured, understandable, and reusable semantic frameworks within this latent space.

Recent breakthroughs in deep learning have generated significant excitement for its application in reversible steganography, a cutting-edge field that combines irreversibility and data fidelity with information-hiding capabilities. Recent research has utilized reversible neural networks and probabilistic prediction models to achieve remarkable accuracy in predicting and modifying host images without compromising quality. Nevertheless, conventional networks are deterministic and incapable of measuring uncertainty, a critical factor often overlooked. In response to this gap, we introduce Bayesian Neural Networks (BNNs) for reversible steganography, an innovative approach that utilizes probabilistic inference and uncertainty quantification. By training BBNs on a diverse set of host images, we establish an uncertainty quantification mechanism that guides the reversible steganography process. Furthermore, we develop a Bayesian hybrid BRR-SU method that integrates BNN with a previously established steganographic technique to achieve superior performance. The results show that this novel approach can not only introduce controlled distortions but also hide secret data while preserving the original host image's integrity. The results of the visual and objective evaluations demonstrate the significant improvement in image fidelity and stego-fidelity, particularly using the BRR-SU method compared to existing Steganography With Neural Embedding (SENE) and Reversible steganography on natural images (RSNI) models.

Our research investigates the implications of the J/ψ decay into invisible matter for light sterile neutrinos and sub-GeV dark matter. We conduct a joint analysis of three effective interactions that can facilitate such decays: neutrino mixing with a sterile state, coupling of dark matter to photons via a Higgs portal, and exchange of a scalar particle between dark matter and electrons that can be mediated by the J/ψ decay. By combining experimental data from KAMIOKANDE, radiation physics experiments, and accelerator studies like GENIe and Mainz, we determine the constraints on these effective interactions as functions of the mediating particle's mass. We further explore how these limits on the J/ψ decay into invisible matter relate to other studies of dark matter production in semileptonic J/ψ decays.

High-resolution observations of the solar photosphere reveal tiny magnetic bright points, which are challenging to study due to their vast abundance and minuscule size. To address this, we analyzed the spatial intensity distributions of magnetic bright points within a 3.42 arcsec by 3.42 arcsec patch of the solar photosphere, captured by the HiRISE instrument on the Hubble Space Telescope. Employing a 2D Kolmogorov-Ostrowski mixture model, we deconvolved the observed distribution into the instrumental point spread function and the intrinsic distribution of magnetic bright points. The resulting model identified a two-component Gamma distribution, with one component reflecting the solar photospheric magnetic bright points and the other representing unphysically large bright points, likely the result of image processing artifacts. This novel two-component data characterization provides valuable insights into the intrinsic properties of solar magnetic bright points, including their size, size range, and average lifespan.

Human vision can distinguish objects and actions using spatial or temporal data, but integrating these aspects remains unclear. This study demonstrates how the human visual system can effectively combine spatial and motion information, enabling recognition in scenarios where individual sources are insufficient. Researchers achieved this insight by analyzing'minimal videos' - brief clips that facilitate reliable object, part, and action recognition, but are unrecognizable when spatial or temporal constraints are compromised. Unlike existing deep networks, which struggle to replicate this integration, humans outperform them in dynamic recognition tasks, highlighting potential improvements for future models.

Dark matter particles that behave like magnetic charges or "monopoles" could potentially generate their own aggregated magnetic fields in space, fields that could stir up chaos within galaxies and disrupt the magnetic fields we observe there. However, new research suggests that monopoles weighing less than a milligram per cubic centimeter and having a magnetic property of less than 17 dec Gauss could coexist with the magnetic fields we see in our galaxy and other galaxies. This means that monopoles with such a low density would produce negligible forces on charged particles, allowing them to travel vast distances without significantly altering the magnetic fields we observe in space. This finding holds true for both our local galaxy and the space between galaxies, suggesting that the existence of these monopoles would not interfere with the magnetic fields we see in space.

This work proposes a novel network, called Uformer, based on the Transformer architecture, for precise meteorological forecasting. Computationally efficient and memory-friendly, Uformer leverages spatial temporal patches to model weather forecasting problems as continuous video prediction tasks, incorporating both spatial and temporal encoders. A novel mechanism, the SWCA module, is introduced to efficiently capture spatiotemporal dependencies, complemented by residual connections and encoders that gradually improve feature representation. Thorough experiments on the Weather421 dataset demonstrate the advantages of our model, which exhibits nearly 15 times faster training time and 3.5 times faster inference time/lower computing cost while maintaining or outperforming current method(s) for weather forecasting.

In a three-Higgs-doublet model with $S_3$ symmetry, we analyze the properties of dark matter within the framework of CP-conserving theories. By introducing labeled fields, we identify two potential dark matter candidates, each supported by distinct viable models. If one dark matter candidate, associated with a field with triplets of states, is selected, the field's wave function must be symmetric. Conversely, the other dark matter candidate, linked to a field with two dark states, corresponds to an antisymmetric wave function. We calculate the masses of these dark states, as well as those of h and $h_\phi$, higgs bosons, to predict potential outcomes of collider experiments and indirect detection searches. In our findings, either dark matter candidate can account for all observed values of the dark matter relic density, while simultaneously remaining compatible with the constraints imposed by electroweak precision observables and future collider and indirect detection experiments.

A comprehensive study on the PPT square conjecture is presented with a notable achievement: the PPT square conjecture's validity has been rigorously demonstrated for the case involving finite-dimensional space.

In order for a neuron to function, it must maintain a balance of various substances
within its different compartments, which can be challenging due to limited membrane
transport options and the complex geometry of its extended branches. To address this issue,
neurons have evolved a unique and highly organized system of intracellular transport,
relying on special cargo, such as mitochondrial DNA and protein complexes, moving along their
branching networks. However, this process is not always efficient, as observed traffic jams,
as seen in neuron imaging of moving bright spots, indicate material shortages in certain areas.
This study presents a mathematical model that uses an optimization approach to regulate
the movement of transported materials, ensuring optimal distribution, and potentially relieving
traffic jams as a byproduct. The model is demonstrated using a simple neuron shape,
showing effective distribution of materials and clearance of previously observed traffic jams.

Billion-dollar losses inflicted by banking fraud across the globe make graph-based fraud detection in transactions increasingly significant. In analyzing transaction patterns, researchers utilize graphs to identify novel and complex schemes. This research aims to identify real-world transaction network patterns, specifically network motifs within a heterogenous transaction dataset. We also present a method for generating genuine network motifs, unlike existing methods which create only a single type of motif shape. Our approach enables the discovery of meaningful and complex network patterns in real datasets, which may provide regulators with a broader understanding of subtle network interactions in banking systems.

In a numerical simulation involving a stellar object falling towards a black hole from within the extended gaseous disk of a white dwarf, significant amounts of energy are produced as the accretion disk is disrupted. This disruption leads to an initial explosion of energy, which gradually stabilizes at a lower level over the course of the simulation. Most of the accreted material remains within the disk plane, whereas a small fraction is ejected, primarily in the form of jets along the axes. The energy output from this process can be comparable to, or even exceed that of various black hole-related phenomena, such as those associated with pulsars, active galactic nuclei, and other black holes, making it a promising area for further observation and study.

Three-body semileptonic tau decets, particularly those involving mildly hadronic final states, can provide precise tests of fundamental physics and detailed information about hadronic currents and form factors. Given that the hadronic currents are linked to light hadron ground states and excited states via spatial wave functions, a systematic and comprehensive understanding of hadron dynamics is necessary to interpret hadronic $\tau$ decays. Unlike the complexities of strong interactions in high-energy hadronic $\tau$ decays, mild hadronic final states predominantly consist of pion pairs, making the application of well-established pion field theories such as the nonlinear and the nonzero sigma models highly applicable. However, the applicability of these models to the analysis of the spatial structures of mild and strong interactions in hadronic tau decays remains an open question, prompting a systematic investigation of hadron dynamics and its relevance to hadronic currents and form factors.

Jim\'enez, Becerra, and Gelbukh proposed the tversky distance in 2014, and Suli\'n in 2018 demonstrated that it relates to the normalized information distance via the formula:
  $\max\left(\alpha,\beta\right)\cdot\operatorname{NID}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B}) = \operatorname{TV}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B})$.
  This paper shows that the left-hand side of this equation is symmetric for all $\alpha$ and $\beta$ if and only that $\alpha + \beta \le 1$.
  The paper also discusses the implications of this finding in relation to equation (1).

This study proposes a novel motion deblurring network, specifically designed for
human and scene deblurring, that overcomes the limitations of traditional
approaches, which are hindered by the inaccuracy of prior art in generating
independent, clear references or sharp stock databases. To overcome these
limitations, we introduce the concept of pseudo-blur, enabling our proposed
method to learn the transformation from blurry to clear images without relying
on labeled paired data. The pseudo-blur is created by iteratively refining a
latent representation, providing an alternative solution to the deblurring
problem. The proposed method demonstrates superior performance compared to
existing approaches using both real blurry images and human and scene datasets
that are not paired, as well as other available datasets.

Hebbian theory aims to explain how neural connections strengthen in the absence of direct evidence, implying a fundamental need for neurons to "learn" about their surrounding environment to form coherent thoughts. This study develops the first biological learning system emulation using a single atom-precise molecular array, emulating a classic Hebbian "correlated firing" neuron model with an if-then rule for synaptic plasticity. The artificial neuron's behavior, modeled after a well-established routing-by-forecasting concept, demonstrates enhanced activity in response to anticipated inputs. Our study demonstrates that storing two distinct sets of molecular keys enables the system to recognize and differentiate between complex environmental patterns, "learning" their unique characteristics to predict subsequent patterns and triggering a response accordingly.

The ultrapower of any ordered set is created as a refined version of the set itself by taking into account infinite sequences of elements from it. This process involves dividing the sequences into classes according to a set of rules defined by an ultrafilter, leading to a set that always satisfies a fundamental property of ordered sets. It turns out that a set's openness determines its ability to fulfill the complete ordered set property after being transformed into a set of elements of a certain type.

We argue for adopting profiling as a crucial step in data analysis and propose the DataUsableUse case profiling approach, focusing on specific datasets. In line with US policy, our work tackles the challenge of balancing data utility with privacy, aiming to identify and recommend data sharing practices that ensure both privacy and utility. Building on existing findings, we introduce an additional category of data value: accuracy, which we believe should complement traditional dataset attributes like modality and distribution. To further our goals, we introduce the DataUsableUse cases, a framework that enables us to elicit data requirements, and propose Utility Accuracy Ratio as a new metric to assess data quality after differential utility degradation.
